case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
title: Meet the Real F-35A
tests: Tests whether a short factual aircraft film preserves the named variant's visible geometry and operating characteristics.

faults.what: The final caption is visibly garbled rather than reading 'Conventional takeoff'.
The aircraft is not a convincing real F-35A: its elongated pointed nose, stretched canopy, wing/body proportions and small rear nozzle give it an inaccurate, synthetic configuration.
Aircraft geometry changes between views, particularly the wing/body shape, tail arrangement and rear fuselage, undermining the appearance of one consistent real aircraft.

judge.summary: The clip shows a runway departure with correct factual narration, but the aircraft is inaccurate and inconsistent and the final caption is garbled.

must_haves.item: The aircraft has the recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear engine exhaust, two outward-canted vertical tails and no canards.
must_haves.why: Twin tails, no obvious canards and a single visible rear nozzle are present, but the overall nose, canopy, fuselage and exhaust proportions do not convincingly represent a real F-35.

must_haves.item: The takeoff shows a forward runway roll and lift-off, not hovering or a vertical launch.
must_haves.why: The successive views show runway rotation followed by increasing clearance and forward climbing flight.

must_haves.item: The same aircraft design remains consistent between the runway and airborne views.
must_haves.why: The wing/body geometry and rear fuselage visibly change across the supplied views.

must_haves.item: All three requested labels appear exactly and are legible.
must_haves.why: The title and 'One engine' are legible and correct, but 'Conventional takeoff' is replaced by garbled text.

must_haves.item: Audible English narration correctly describes one engine and conventional runway takeoff without attributing F-35B hover capability to the F-35A.
must_haves.why: The supplied speech transcript explicitly states that the F-35A has one engine and makes a conventional runway takeoff, with no hover claim.
